questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: What is the average of 18, 25, 32 and 41?
hints: Add all the numbers first.
Divide the total by how many numbers there are.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: Kitty saved $12 on Monday, $15 on Tuesday, nothing on Wednesday, $18 on Thursday and $20 on Friday. What was her average saving per day from Monday to Friday?
hints: Wednesday's $0 still counts as one day.
Total saving ÷ 5 days.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: Which of the following groups of numbers has an average of 20?
hints: For each group, add the numbers and divide by how many there are.
Careful: some groups have 3 numbers, some have 4.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: The average age of 6 members of a club is 24.5. A new member aged 35 joins the club. What is the new average age of the members?
hints: Find the total age of the 6 members first.
Add the new member, then divide by the NEW number of members.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 36. The average of the first four numbers is 33.5. What is the fifth number?
hints: Total of 5 numbers = 5 × 36.
Total of first four = 4 × 33.5. Subtract.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: Grace's average mark in 3 tests is 78. She wants her average mark to be 80 or above after the 4th test. At least how many marks must she get in the 4th test?
hints: What total is needed for an average of 80 in 4 tests?
Subtract the total she already has.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: One number is removed from the group 9, 15, 21, 27, 33 and the average decreases by 1.5. Which number is removed?
hints: Find the old average and the old total.
New total = new average × 4. The difference is the removed number.
questions.working: Old average 105 ÷ 5 = 21; new average 19.5; new total 19.5 × 4 = 78; removed 105 − 78 = 27

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: The average weight of 4 boxes is 2.35 kg. A fifth box weighing 2.8 kg is added. What is the new average weight of the boxes?
hints: Total of 4 boxes = 4 × 2.35 kg.
Add 2.8 kg and divide by 5.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: Mr Chan spends $250 each day from Monday to Friday and $460 each day on Saturday and Sunday. What is his average daily expense in that week?
hints: There are 5 weekdays and 2 weekend days.
Find the week's total, then divide by 7 (not by 2!).

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: The average of A, B and C is 72. C is 96 and A is 3 times B. Find the value of A.
hints: Find A + B + C, then A + B.
If A is 3 times B, then A + B is 4 equal parts.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: In a class, the average weight of 12 boys is 45 kg and the average weight of the girls is 40 kg. The average weight of the whole class is 42.4 kg. How many girls are there in the class?
hints: Each boy is 45 − 42.4 kg ABOVE the class average.
Each girl is 42.4 − 40 kg BELOW it. The 'above' and 'below' amounts must balance.
questions.working: Boys above: 12 × 2.6 = 31.2 kg; each girl below by 2.4 kg; girls = 31.2 ÷ 2.4 = 13

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: Mabel's average distance in 5 long jumps is 3.4 m. The average of her first three jumps is 3.3 m. Her 4th jump is 0.2 m longer than her 5th jump. How long is her 5th jump?
hints: Find the total of all 5 jumps and of the first 3 jumps.
The last two jumps add to the difference. The 4th is 0.2 m more than the 5th.

questions.category: T9 Average (mean): new average, missing value, combined groups
questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 45. When one of the numbers, 30, is changed to another number, the average becomes 48. What is the new number?
hints: How much bigger is the new total than the old total?
The changed number grew by exactly that amount.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A measuring cup contains 300 mL of water. After a stone is put in and sinks completely, the water level reads 375 mL. What is the volume of the stone?
hints: The stone pushes the water up by its own volume.
1 mL = 1 cm³.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A rectangular tank is 25 cm long and 16 cm wide. It contains water 8 cm deep. After a stone is put in and sinks completely, the water level rises to 11 cm. What is the volume of the stone?
hints: How many cm did the water rise?
Volume of stone = length × width × rise.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A cuboid container has a base of 15 cm × 13 cm. Ivy pours in 1.2 L of water and then 3 cups of 250 mL of water. What is the height of the water?
hints: Change everything to mL (1 L = 1000 mL), and 1 mL = 1 cm³.
Height = volume ÷ base area.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: 2 L of water is poured into an empty container with a square base of side 20 cm. What is the height of the water?
hints: Base area of a square = side × side.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A cubic jug of side 20 cm is full of juice. The juice is poured into an empty tank 25 cm × 16 cm × 15 cm until the tank is full. How much juice is left in the jug? (Give your answer in L.)
hints: Find the volume of the jug and the capacity of the tank.
Left = jug − tank. 1,000 cm³ = 1 L.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A fish tank is 1.2 m long, 0.8 m wide and 1 m high. When a rock is put in, the water level rises by 0.05 m. What is the volume of the rock in m³?
hints: Volume of rock = length × width × rise.
The height of the tank (1 m) is not needed.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A tank has a base of 40 cm × 25 cm and contains water 18 cm deep. An iron cube of side 10 cm is put in and sinks completely. What is the new height of the water?
hints: Volume of the cube = 10 × 10 × 10.
Rise = volume of cube ÷ base area of the tank. Add it to 18 cm.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: An open wooden box (no cover) measures 30 cm × 20 cm × 12 cm on the outside. The wood is 1 cm thick. What is the capacity of the box in litres?
hints: Length and width lose the thickness on BOTH sides.
An open box has no cover, so the height loses the thickness only once (the bottom).

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A container has a base area of 600 cm². When 5 identical marbles are put in (fully under water), the water level rises by 0.8 cm. What is the volume of each marble?
hints: Volume of all marbles = base area × rise.
Then share by 5.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A cuboid container 20 cm long, 10 cm wide and 15 cm high holds water 13 cm deep. Identical stones, each 45 cm³, are put in one by one and sink completely. At least how many stones must be put in to make the water overflow?
hints: Find the empty space above the water.
To OVERFLOW, the stones must be more than the empty space.
questions.working: Space = 20 × 10 × 2 = 400 cm³; 400 ÷ 45 = 8 r 40; 8 stones fill 360 cm³ (no overflow), so 9 stones are needed.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: A cuboid container 12 cm long, 10 cm wide and 20 cm high holds water 16 cm deep. Marbles of 30 cm³ each are put in and sink. At most how many marbles can be put in WITHOUT the water spilling?
hints: Find the empty space above the water.
If the marbles exactly fill the space, the water reaches the brim but does not spill.
questions.working: Space = 12 × 10 × 4 = 480 cm³; 480 ÷ 30 = 16 exactly → 16 marbles (water just reaches the top).

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: An aquarium has a base of 50 cm × 30 cm and contains water 20 cm deep. After 3 identical air pumps are put in (fully under water), the water level rises to 21.2 cm. What is the volume of each air pump?
hints: Volume of 3 pumps = base area × rise, then ÷ 3.

questions.category: T12 Water level: displacement, height of liquid, thickness/inner capacity
questions.question: An open steel container (no cover) measures 28 cm × 20 cm × 15 cm on the outside. The steel is 2 cm thick. What is the capacity of the container?
hints: Length and width: subtract 2 cm on each side.
Height: an open container only has a bottom, so subtract 2 cm once.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: A pencil costs $4.60. Jenny buys 3 pencils and pays with a $20 note. How much change should she get?
hints: Find the cost of 3 pencils.
Change = money paid − cost.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: The same can of soup is sold in four ways. Which is the best buy (cheapest per can)?
hints: Find the price of ONE can for each brand.
The smallest price per can is the best buy.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: A pen costs $5.60. A shop offers 'Buy 4, get 1 free'. Joe gets 5 pens under the offer. Compared with the usual price, how much cheaper is each pen?
hints: He pays for only 4 pens but gets 5.
Find the cost of each of the 5 pens, then compare with $5.60.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: A buffet costs $268 per adult and $168 per child. A group of 35 people goes to the buffet, and 2/7 of them are children. How much does the group pay altogether?
hints: Find the number of children, then the number of adults.
Multiply each by its price and add.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: 1.5 kg of cherries cost $72. Mrs Ma buys 2.5 kg of the same cherries and pays with $150. How much change does she get?
hints: Find the price of 1 kg first.
Cost of 2.5 kg, then subtract from $150.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: 7 notebooks cost the same as 4 files. A file costs $15.75. How much does a notebook cost?
hints: Find the cost of 4 files.
That money buys 7 notebooks — share it by 7.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: Taxi fares: the first 2 km (or any part thereof) costs $29. Every subsequent 200 m (or part thereof) costs $2.10. Mr Ho travels 4.5 km by taxi. How much is the fare?
hints: Distance after the first 2 km, in metres.
'Or part thereof' means a part of 200 m is counted as a whole 200 m — round UP.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: A laundry charges $36 for the first 3 kg of clothes, and $5.80 for every additional 0.5 kg (or part thereof). Mrs Wong washes 5.2 kg of clothes. How much does she pay?
hints: How many kg are over the first 3 kg?
How many 0.5 kg parts is that? A part counts as a whole one.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: A mobile phone plan charges $78 for the first 800 minutes of airtime, and $0.25 per minute after that. Mr Lee's bill is $123.50. How many minutes of airtime did he use?
hints: How much of the bill is for the extra minutes?
Extra minutes = extra money ÷ $0.25. Don't forget the first 800 minutes.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: Gas charges: the first 100 units cost $1.80 per unit; the next 200 units cost $1.60 per unit; each unit above 300 units costs $1.40. A family used 450 units. How much is the gas bill?
hints: Split 450 units into the three parts: 100, 200 and the rest.
Charge each part at its own price, then add.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: A car park charges $24 for the first hour and $9 for each subsequent half hour (or part thereof). Mr Tse parks from 9:15 a.m. to 12:40 p.m. How much does he pay?
hints: Find how long he parked, then take away the first hour.
Count the half hours left — a part of a half hour counts as a whole one.

questions.category: T16 Money, best buy & tiered charges (taxi, laundry, phone, gas, buffet, bills)
questions.question: Boxes of juice are sold at $10.50 each or $57 for a pack of 6. Ms Lam needs exactly 14 boxes. What is the least amount she must pay?
hints: One box in a pack costs $57 ÷ 6. Is that cheaper than $10.50?
Buy as many packs as you can without going over 14, then buy single boxes. Check whether one extra pack is cheaper.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: How many faces does a pentagonal prism have?
hints: A prism has 2 bases plus one side face for each side of the base.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: Which of the following solids has NO vertex?
hints: A vertex is a corner point.
A cone has one pointed tip — that is a vertex.
questions.working: A cylinder has only curved edges and no corner, so it has no vertex.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: A cylinder is cut by a plane parallel to its base. What is the shape of the cross-section?
hints: Cutting parallel to the base gives the same shape as the base.
questions.working: The base of a cylinder is a circle, so the cross-section is a circle.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: The net of a prism is made up of 2 hexagons and some rectangles. How many rectangles are there?
hints: Each side of the hexagon base joins one rectangle.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: Which of the following solids has the same number of vertices as a pentagonal prism?
hints: A pentagonal prism has 5 vertices on top and 5 at the bottom.
A pyramid with an n-sided base has n + 1 vertices.
questions.working: Pentagonal prism: 10 vertices. Hexagonal pyramid 7, nonagonal pyramid 10, pentagonal pyramid 6, hexagonal prism 12.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: Sam makes a model of an octagonal prism using plasticine balls as vertices and sticks as edges. Each ball costs $0.80 and each stick costs $1.50. How much do the balls and sticks cost altogether?
hints: Balls = vertices, sticks = edges.
An octagonal prism has 2 × 8 vertices and 3 × 8 edges.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: Lily has 9 plasticine balls and 12 sticks. She wants to make a model of a hexagonal prism. How many more balls and how many more sticks does she need?
hints: Count the vertices (balls) and edges (sticks) of a hexagonal prism.
Subtract what she already has.
questions.working: Hexagonal prism: 12 vertices, 18 edges. 12 − 9 = 3 balls; 18 − 12 = 6 sticks.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: Ben uses exactly 15 sticks and 10 plasticine balls to make a 3-D model. What could the model be?
hints: Sticks = edges, balls = vertices.
Check edges AND vertices of each option.
questions.working: Pentagonal prism: 15 edges, 10 vertices ✓ (pentagonal pyramid 10/6, decagonal pyramid 20/11, hexagonal pyramid 12/7).

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: A square pyramid is cut by a plane parallel to its base. What is the shape of the cross-section?
hints: A cut parallel to the base gives a smaller copy of the base.
Cutting through the apex would give a triangle — but this cut is parallel to the base.
questions.working: Parallel to a square base → a (smaller) square.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: A pyramid has 9 faces. How many edges does it have?
hints: A pyramid has 1 base face plus one triangle for each side of the base.
Edges = 2 × number of sides of the base.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: A square pyramid is placed exactly on top of a cube so that the base of the pyramid covers the top face of the cube. How many faces and how many edges does the new solid have?
hints: The top face of the cube and the base of the pyramid are hidden — they are no longer faces.
The 4 edges where they join are shared, so count them only once.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: A cube is cut into two identical solids by a plane passing through two opposite vertical edges (along the diagonal of the top face). Name each solid and state how many edges it has.
hints: Look at the top face: the diagonal cuts the square into two triangles.
Triangle on top, same triangle at the bottom, straight sides — what prism is that?
questions.working: Each part has two triangular bases and three rectangular faces: a triangular prism with 3 × 3 = 9 edges.

questions.category: T13 3-D shapes: faces/edges/vertices, balls & sticks, nets, cross-sections
questions.question: A prism has 21 edges. How many vertices does it have?
hints: A prism with an n-sided base has 3 × n edges.
Find n, then vertices = 2 × n.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: There are 245 students in a school hall. 3/7 of them are girls. How many boys are there?
hints: Find the number of girls first, or find the fraction that are boys.
Boys = 1 − 3/7 of the students.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: There was 1,500 mL of juice in a jug. Tom drank 1/4 of it and Mary drank 1/6 of it. How much juice was left?
hints: Both fractions are of the SAME 1,500 mL, so you can add them.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: There are 420 passengers on a ship. 3/10 of them are men and 2/7 of them are women. The rest are children. How many children are there?
hints: Find the number of men and the number of women.
Children = 420 − men − women.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: The distance from A to B is 96 km. The distance from B to C is 3/8 shorter than the distance from A to B. What is the total distance from A to C through B?
hints: '3/8 shorter' means B to C is (1 − 3/8) of 96 km.
Add the two distances.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: There are 120 flowers. 2/3 of them are roses, and 3/5 of the roses are red. Which expression gives the number of roses that are NOT red?
hints: Number of roses = 120 × 2/3.
Not red is (1 − 3/5) of the roses.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: A bag costs $180. A wallet costs $54 less than the bag. What fraction of the price of the bag is the price of the wallet?
hints: Find the price of the wallet first.
Fraction = wallet ÷ bag. Simplify.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: Mrs Yip had 3 3/4 L of milk. After making some cakes, 1 1/2 L of milk was left. Each cake needs 3/8 L of milk. How many cakes did she make?
hints: Find how much milk was used.
Number of cakes = milk used ÷ 3/8.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: A shop had 240 shirts. It sold 3/8 of them and donated 2/5 of the remaining shirts to a charity. How many shirts were left?
hints: Find how many were sold and how many REMAINED.
2/5 is a fraction of the remainder, not of 240.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: Kelvin had 96 stamps. He gave away 5/12 of them and then sold 14 stamps. What fraction of his stamps was left?
hints: Find how many he gave away, then subtract that and the 14 sold.
Write stamps left over 96 and simplify.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: A bakery made 1,260 cupcakes. 4/7 of them were sold. 5/12 of the cupcakes sold were chocolate. How many of the cupcakes sold were NOT chocolate?
hints: Find the number sold first.
Not chocolate = 1 − 5/12 of the sold cupcakes.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: In a fruit box, 1/3 of the fruits are oranges, 2/5 are apples and the rest are 28 pears. How many fruits are there in the box?
hints: What fraction of the fruits are pears?
If that fraction is 28 fruits, find the whole.

questions.category: T8 Fraction word problems (fraction of a quantity, of the remainder, "what fraction")
questions.question: There was 2 2/5 L of soy sauce in a bottle. Chef Lau took 5/8 of it, and used 2/3 of what he took. How much soy sauce did he use?
hints: First find 5/8 of 2 2/5 L.
Then find 2/3 of that amount.

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the midday temperature of a city in a week. What is the difference between the highest and the lowest temperature?
hints: Find the highest point and the lowest point on the graph.
Subtract.

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the numbers of A-Pads and B-Pads sold by a shop from January to June. In which month were the same numbers of A-Pads and B-Pads sold?
hints: Look for the month where the two lines meet.
questions.working: In March both lines are at 40.

data.title: Number of Tablets Sold by a Shop

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the rainfall of a city from January to June. In which month was the rainfall 70 mm less than in May?
hints: Read May's rainfall, then subtract 70 mm.
Find the month with that reading.

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows Mrs Kwok's daily expenses in a week. On which two days did her expenses differ by $160?
hints: Read the expense for each day in the options.
Subtract to find each difference.

data.title: Mrs Kwok's Daily Expenses in a Week

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the midday temperature of a city in a week. Between which two consecutive days was the change in temperature the greatest?
hints: Look for the steepest line segment (up or down).
Work out each day-to-day change to check.
questions.working: Changes: +3, −1, −4, +1, +5, −3 → greatest is Friday to Saturday (5 °C).

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the midday temperature of a city in a week. What was the average midday temperature of that week?
hints: Read all 7 temperatures carefully.
Add them and divide by 7.

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the numbers of A-Pads and B-Pads sold by a shop from January to June. In which month was the number of A-Pads sold twice the number of B-Pads sold?
hints: For each month, double the B-Pad number.
Compare it with the A-Pad number.

data.title: Number of Tablets Sold by a Shop

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the numbers of A-Pads and B-Pads sold by a shop from January to June. How many A-Pads were sold in the first half of the year?
hints: The first half of the year is January to June.
Use only the A-Pad line.

data.title: Number of Tablets Sold by a Shop

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the numbers of A-Pads and B-Pads sold by a shop from January to June. Each B-Pad was sold at $2,400. How much money was received from selling B-Pads in May?
hints: Read the number of B-Pads sold in May.
Multiply by $2,400.

data.title: Number of Tablets Sold by a Shop

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the numbers of A-Pads and B-Pads sold by a shop from January to June. What was the average number of B-Pads sold per month from January to June?
hints: Add the six B-Pad readings.
Divide by 6.

data.title: Number of Tablets Sold by a Shop

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the rainfall of a city from January to June. Compared with the month before, which month had the greatest increase in rainfall?
hints: Find the increase from each month to the next.
The steepest upward segment shows the greatest increase.

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows the rainfall of a city from January to June. What is the average rainfall of the two months with the most rainfall?
hints: Find the two highest points.
Add them and divide by 2.

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows Mrs Kwok's daily expenses in a week. What was her average daily expense in that week?
hints: Add the expenses of all 7 days.
Divide by 7.

data.title: Mrs Kwok's Daily Expenses in a Week

questions.category: T17 Broken line graphs
questions.question: The broken line graph shows Mrs Kwok's daily expenses in a week. What fraction of her total expense in that week was spent on Saturday?
hints: Find the week's total first.
Saturday ÷ total, then simplify.

data.title: Mrs Kwok's Daily Expenses in a Week

questions.category: T5 Division with remainder in context ("at most how many", "how much is left", "how many needed")
questions.question: 3.5 L of soup is poured into bowls of 0.4 L each. At most how many bowls can be filled, and how much soup is left?
hints: How many 0.4 L fit into 3.5 L without going over?
Left = 3.5 − (bowls × 0.4).

questions.category: T15 Algebra: expressing quantities with letters
questions.question: A school hires 18 large coaches with 45 seats each and n small coaches with 20 seats each. At most how many students can the coaches carry? (Answer in terms of n.)
hints: Large coaches carry 18 × 45 students.
Small coaches carry 20 × n.

questions.category: T15 Algebra: expressing quantities with letters
questions.question: A pen costs $p. A notebook costs $3 more than the pen. How much do 4 notebooks cost?
hints: One notebook costs $(p + 3).
Multiply EVERYTHING in the bracket by 4.

questions.category: T15 Algebra: expressing quantities with letters
questions.question: Ann had a stickers. After giving 7 stickers to Ben, she had 25 stickers left. Find a.
hints: Write the equation: a − 7 = 25.
Undo the subtraction by adding 7.

questions.question: Solve the equation 3y + 5 = 26.
hints: First take away 5 from both sides.
Then divide by 3.

questions.category: T19 Directions & turning
questions.question: Peter is facing north. He turns 1 right angle clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
hints: Clockwise goes N → E → S → W.
1 right angle = 90°.

questions.category: T19 Directions & turning
questions.question: A robot is facing south-east. It turns 1 right angle anticlockwise. Which direction is it facing now?
hints: Anticlockwise goes the opposite way to clock hands.
90° from south-east anticlockwise passes east.

questions.category: T19 Directions & turning
questions.question: Sue stands with her back facing north. She turns 2 right angles clockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
hints: If your back faces north, you are facing the opposite way.
2 right angles = a half turn.

questions.category: T19 Directions & turning
questions.question: Mary's right-hand side is facing south. She then turns 3 right angles anticlockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
hints: If your right hand points south, which way are you facing?
Anticlockwise 3 right angles = 270° to the left.
questions.working: Right side south → facing east; 270° anticlockwise → south

questions.category: T19 Directions & turning
questions.question: Jason is facing west. He turns 270° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
hints: 270° = 3 right angles.
Count W → N → E → S.

questions.category: T19 Directions & turning
questions.question: Kelly is facing north-west. She turns 135° clockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
hints: Each step between neighbouring directions (e.g. N to NE) is 45°.
135° = 3 steps.

questions.category: T19 Directions & turning
questions.question: Tom is facing east. He turns clockwise until he faces north. What is the smallest angle he has turned?
hints: Clockwise from east goes to south first.
Count the right angles from east to north going clockwise.
questions.working: E → S → W → N = 3 right angles = 270°

questions.category: T19 Directions & turning
questions.question: Leo is facing north-east. He turns 3 right angles anticlockwise and then 1 right angle clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
hints: 3 anticlockwise and 1 clockwise = 2 right angles anticlockwise altogether.
2 right angles is a half turn.
